Senses.Explanation: A verb phrase: “awaken” plus “the Way.” Chan records use it retrospectively in biographies and cases: Lingyun awakens on seeing peach blossoms, the Buddha on seeing the morning star, and other monks after an encounter or event; verses composed afterward are called “verses on awakening to the Way.” The stock pairing “awaken to the Way on hearing a sound; clarify mind on seeing a form” is itself raised and questioned in a hall address. The records also police the designation: one text calls memorizing two convenient sayings and naming that “awakening to the Way” one of the enumerated kinds of foolish Chan. Thus the term names an attested event and biographical verdict, while the corpus also records challenges to loose claims of it.
Senses.Note: The compound “verse on awakening to the Way” retains the same event sense and is not a separate referent for “awaken to the Way” itself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉古云聞聲悟道見色明心師云作麼生是聞聲悟道見色明心
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address raises the old saying “awaken to the Way on hearing sound; clarify mind on seeing form” and asks what that is.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人見桃華悟道，子作麼生？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huanglong asks about the old case of awakening to the Way on seeing peach blossoms.

Occurrences.Kwic: 忽然大悟乃有悟道頌云我有明珠一顆久被諸塵封褁
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A retrospective reports sudden great awakening and introduces a “verse on awakening to the Way.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 或有向古人方便語中記得兩句，謂之悟道，謂之通宗
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanlai criticizes those who memorize two convenient sayings of the ancients and call it “awakening to the Way” and “penetrating the school.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 十二月八日明星現時，豁然悟道，大地有情，一時成佛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address deploys the Buddha as a Chan figure by recounting his awakening to the Way when the morning star appeared.
